data.name: Reverse_NoTargetClasses
data.value: No classes to reverse were found. Select a .g.cs that holds the generated entities (Entities.g.cs with split output) and was generated with IncludeDataAnnotations ON, so that the classes carry the [Table] attribute.

data.name: Reverse_TableWithoutColumns
data.value: Table '{0}' was reversed with no columns, because none of its properties could be restored as a column.

data.name: Reverse_PrimaryKeyColumnMissingTypeMeta
data.value: Primary key column '{0}.{1}' has no DB type metadata ([DbColumnMeta]) and was skipped, so table '{0}' is reversed without that primary key column.

data.name: Reverse_RelationshipColumnUnresolved
data.value: Column '{0}.{1}' of the relationship '{2}' -> '{3}' could not be resolved, so the relationship was restored without a column pair (it takes no part in DDL generation or schema diffs).

data.name: Reverse_NavigationUnreadable
data.value: The [NavigationReference] on '{0}.{1}' could not be read (its endpoint arguments are missing, are not string literals, or are named arguments in another order), so the relationship was ignored.

data.name: Reverse_NavigationTableMissing
data.value: The relationship '{0}' -> '{1}' was ignored, because table '{2}' is not among the reversed tables.

data.name: Reverse_DuplicateTable
data.value: Table name '{0}' is declared by more than one class; every one of them was reversed, so the diagram holds several tables with that name.

data.name: Reverse_DuplicateColumn
data.value: Column name '{1}' is declared more than once on table '{0}'; every one of them was reversed, so the table holds several columns with that name.

data.name: Reverse_PartialClassSplit
data.value: Class '{0}' is declared as several partial parts in this file, and only the part carrying [Table] is read; {1} column property(ies) declared in the other parts were skipped. Move them into the part that carries [Table].

data.name: Reverse_VerbatimTypeMismatch
data.value: The native type '{0}' recorded for column '{1}.{2}' does not mean the same as its type token '{3}' in the target dialect, so the token was used instead.

data.name: Reverse_SyntaxErrors
data.value: The C# source has {0} syntax error(s), so it cannot be reversed safely (a truncated or partially pasted file would silently lose columns). Fix the source and try again. First errors: {1}

data.name: Reverse_ColumnMissingTypeMeta
data.value: Column '{0}.{1}' has no DB type metadata ([DbColumnMeta]) and was skipped.

data.name: Reverse_TypeTokenUnresolved
data.value: Type token '{0}' for column '{1}.{2}' could not be expanded for the target dialect; using it verbatim.

data.name: Reverse_UniqueConstraintMemberUnresolved
data.value: A UNIQUE constraint on table '{0}' refers to property '{1}', which is not a restored column; the whole constraint was skipped.

data.name: Reverse_UniqueConstraintEmpty
data.value: A UNIQUE constraint on table '{0}' declares no member property and was skipped.

data.name: Reverse_ReferentialActionUnknown
data.value: Referential action '{0}' on the relationship '{1}' -> '{2}' is unknown; it was left unspecified (NO ACTION).
